pointers.sentence: What it must write is the difference, as operations, and the autodetector finds it by comparing the two states: it is given no connection and reads no database (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector`).

`MigrationAutodetector.changes` is given the graph and, optionally, a set of labels to trim the result to, a set of labels to convert, which lets an application with no migrations be given its first, and a name for the new migrations (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.changes`).

Two commands make an autodetector. makemigrations gives it the two states and a questioner, and passes the labels on its command line as both sets ([The makemigrations command](makemigrations.md)). migrate makes one with no questioner, and only where its plan is empty and its verbosity is not 0: if `changes` returns anything, it prints the labels in a notice that the models have changes no migration has yet (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`; [The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](migrate.md)).
`MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes` first sorts the models (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes`).

The from-state's `ProjectState.real_apps` holds the labels of the unmigrated applications, which the loader passes to it; no migration made their models, and the from-state has none of them (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.project_state`).
With no leaf node in the graph, `MigrationGraph.make_state` returns a project state whose `real_apps` is empty (`django/db/migrations/graph.py:MigrationGraph.make_state`).

The release notes say that makemigrations now tracks all changes to unmanaged models, and that it will detect new migrations for those that have changed since they were created (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

A generator returns nothing: it gives each operation to `MigrationAutodetector.add_operation`, which adds it to its application's list in `MigrationAutodetector.generated_operations` and sets on it the dependencies the generator named, each a model or a field and what must first have become of it (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.add_operation`).
Two fields cannot be compared with `==`: a field's equality compares creation counters and models, its place and not its definition (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.__eq__`).

What can be compared is what `Field.deconstruct` returns, the path of the class and the arguments that would make the field again ([A field: the base class](../models/fields.md)), and `MigrationAutodetector.deep_deconstruct` is that, carried all the way down (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.deep_deconstruct`).
A compiled regular expression becomes a `RegexObject`, equal to another of the same pattern and flags (`django/db/migrations/utils.py:RegexObject`).

`MigrationAutodetector.only_relation_agnostic_fields` is a coarser view of a whole model, used to recognise a rename: the deep deconstructions of its fields, in the order of the fields' names and without the names (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.only_relation_agnostic_fields`).

`MigrationAutodetector.generate_renamed_models` looks, for each added model, among the removed models of the same application for one with equal `MigrationAutodetector.only_relation_agnostic_fields`, and on a match asks the questioner's `MigrationQuestioner.ask_rename_model` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_renamed_models`).

It adds a `CreateModel` without the model's relations, a primary key and a parent link excepted, and then, each an operation of its own, an `AddField` for each relation left out, an `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` for `"order_with_respect_to"`, an `AddIndex` for each index, an `AddConstraint` for each constraint and an `AlterUniqueTogether` for `"unique_together"` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_created_models`).

The added models are sorted by `MigrationAutodetector.swappable_first_key`, which, by its docstring, places models that may be swapped, the one `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names among them, first in the lists of created models (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.swappable_first_key`).

For a new proxy `MigrationAutodetector.generate_created_proxies` adds a `CreateModel` with no fields, and for one removed `MigrationAutodetector.generate_deleted_proxies` adds a `DeleteModel` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_created_proxies`).

For each removed model `MigrationAutodetector.generate_deleted_models` adds an `AlterUniqueTogether` that empties `"unique_together"` where there is one, a `RemoveIndex` for each index, a `RemoveConstraint` for each constraint, a `RemoveField` for every relation, primary key and parent link included, and last the `DeleteModel` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_deleted_models`).

Among the keys of `ALTER_OPTION_KEYS` are `"managed"`, `"ordering"`, `"permissions"` and `"verbose_name"`; the docstring of `generate_altered_options` calls such options non-schema-affecting, kept in the state in case Python code in migrations needs them (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_options`).

The lists of managers are compared with `!=`, and a manager is equal to an instance of its class that was made with the same arguments (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_managers`, `django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager.__eq__`).

The lists of managers are compared with `!=`, and a manager is equal to an instance of its class that was made with the same arguments (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_managers`, `django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager.__eq__`).
